Notes

A shaving cut triggers an imperial emergency; a city’s grandeur becomes pettiness; clothes hide animals or nothing at all. A chain of bodily rhymes eventually pulls the whole strange world back into school.

太医

太医 is an imperial physician. Calling for one after a razor nick turns a tiny bathroom mishap into a palace emergency. 不治身亡 then supplies the formal wording for a death despite treatment, as if the scene needs a news report too. “A bunch of quacks” finally punctures the solemn language with ordinary abuse.

  • Chinese lyric transcript (Genius community)
擦亮双眼

擦亮 means polish or wipe until bright. Applied to the eyes, it means become discerning and do not be fooled. The confident declaration is immediately tested by suspicious friends and a subway with no destination displayed. Across the song, claims of clear sight repeatedly run into situations whose meaning or direction remains obscure.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
国际小心眼

大都市 is a metropolis, literally a “big city.” 小心眼 means petty or small-minded, literally a “small mind/heart.” Repeating 国际, “international,” makes the second line sound like another civic accolade while reversing 大, big, into 小, small.

  • Chinese lyric transcript (Genius community)
没写终点

The train is ordinary urban infrastructure, but taking one at random without a displayed terminus removes the part that would make the journey purposeful. After the confident future-facing lines, this small practical absence unsettles the promise. Movement continues without a clear destination, much like the verse’s jumps between street life, secrecy and school memory.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
有点咸有点噎

The repeated 有点 makes the dinner complaint sound casual and manageable. 噎 is the uncomfortable catching of food in the throat, so the ordinary bowl of noodles adds another constricted body to this stretch of the mixtape. Its scale is deliberately small beside imperial death and an “international metropolis”: a bad evening includes something as undramatic as dinner.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
孙子

The following “I’m your granddad” makes 孙子, “grandson,” an insult aimed at people stealing from the speaker. Claiming the senior generation establishes a taunting hierarchy. Read together, these are not lines about a missing grandchild.

  • Chinese lyric transcript (Genius community)
一级的秘密

A private wish is promoted into classified information. 绝不能, “absolutely must not,” just before it and “no ordinary game” afterward keep raising the stakes. The speaker’s desire is now something that has to be defended from other people knowing it; later, “Topboy” will put ideas into a literal safe.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
处心积虑

处心积虑 describes sustained, deliberate planning with a strongly disapproving force: someone has been working out their scheme. It is heavier than a momentary bad impulse. Paired with 人面兽心, the polished four-character idioms make the distrust sound like a verdict, before the verse jumps back into a coarse complaint about money being tight.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
人面兽心

人面兽心 describes a person whose outwardly human appearance conceals cruelty: a human face and a beast’s heart. The next fox-fur coat changes where the animal is located, putting it on the outside as clothing. That progression makes appearance and what lies underneath central to the passage.

  • Chinese lyric transcript (Genius community)
  • Ministry of Education idiom dictionary: 人面獸心
日妈吃紧

吃紧 means strained or in short supply; when applied to one’s days or livelihood, it suggests a financial or practical squeeze. 日妈 is a coarse regional swear inserted as an intensifier. The line’s pressure comes from the combination of a fairly sober word for scarcity and an angry spoken interruption.

  • Chinese lyric transcript (Genius community)
皇帝的新衣

In Andersen’s tale, grown-ups pretend that an emperor’s nonexistent clothes are real until a child says what everybody can see. The following instruction here is to keep a childlike heart. Childhood becomes a way of exposing the performance around you, while the fox-fur coat and human-faced beast have already made clothing and appearances untrustworthy.

  • Hans Christian Andersen Centre: The Emperor’s New Clothes
哥谭

哥谭 is Gotham, Batman’s fictional city, whose crime and corruption are central to DC’s setting. 泥潭, a muddy pool, also describes a predicament someone is stuck in. Before the rhyme narrows to one teacher’s spit, the lyric briefly gives the everyday “same old shit” the scale of a whole corrupted city.

  • Chinese lyric transcript (Genius community)
  • DC: Batman’s Gotham City
痰

The ending stretches the vowel chain 痰 tán, 胆 dǎn, 烂 làn, 蛋 dàn: phlegm, guts, rotten/bad, egg. Each new image provides the syllable for the next stuttered block. The English preserves the changing words and repetitions, but cannot keep that Mandarin rhyme intact.

  • Chinese lyric transcript (Genius community)
吓破胆

吓破胆 literally makes fright break the gallbladder; 胆 also supplies Chinese vocabulary for courage. The phrase gives the ending its next detachable rhyme, dǎn after tán, phlegm. A bodily idiom becomes a sound to repeat, just as the teacher’s spit becomes disproportionately powerful in the school memory.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
太苦了

苦 can describe a bitter taste or a painful, difficult experience. Placed after the teacher’s phlegm, it keeps disgust in the mouth while becoming an explanation for bad grades. The verse turns school failure into a grotesque sensory anecdote, then lets 烂, “bad/rotten,” become another repeated rhyme word.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)

About Jackzebra and this mixtape

Zhuang Zhuang Mixtape arrived on Surf Gang on October 2, 2026: 55 tracks, opening with Sour and closing with Sweet. Its cast widens from YoungQueenz on Poker Face to User116, Effie, kuru, yoyi, 春 and 南部犯罪份子. Aghast has a production credit on every track from Hitman through Snatch, giving that stretch a shared collaborator behind its changing scenes.

Surf Gang release · Artist credits

Jackzebra told AVYSS that he writes while singing over a beat he has listened to repeatedly, keeping the images in his head central. He values the room Mandarin leaves for indirect meanings. Listen for ordinary phrases becoming physical scenes: familiarity becomes cooking, authority becomes family seniority, and a tired saying suddenly turns into a threat.

AVYSS interview, 2024

In STATIC, he describes mixtapes as a format for letting ideas flow, reserving an official debut album for later. In a separate conversation about Above & Beyond, he compared that earlier tape to a collection of his producer friends’ work. The credits here likewise reward attention: long-running collaborators sit alongside guests working in Mandarin, Korean and English.

STATIC interview · Sabukaru interview, 2025

The small details connect to his stated interests: he has described playing Temple Run in transit and before shows, watching Top Boy, and wanting to score White Oleander. These give the songs specific points of contact with his life. The notes follow those connections alongside the lyrics’ jokes, invented scenes and competing voices.

His recommendations in Perfectly Imperfect · Dazed interview, 2025 · Interview questionnaire, 2025

Jackzebra has pushed back on being made to represent all of China’s underground. These notes stay close to the words: what an expression usually means, what changes in this line, and how another song answers it. Cultural references have sources; interpretations rest on details you can hear or read in the song.
